title: Tech Note: Recursion by Example
author: Cha Yang
featured_technology: Object method On Data Change event

historical_commentary.text: Cha Yang (4D, Inc. Technical Engineer) gives a general-purpose introduction to recursion in 4D's classic language, first with a simple `RecursiveFactorial` method, then with a real-world `NumToText` method (originally by Dave Batton of DataCraft, from the 4D NUG) that converts a dollar amount into words for check-printing, and closes with guidance on when recursion helps versus when an iterative loop is preferable due to stack overhead. Recursion is a fundamental, language-agnostic technique and 4D's support for recursive method calls is essentially unchanged since 2001, so the explanations, the stack-overhead caveats, and even the NumToText example remain directly applicable to 4D developers today, in both classic Design Mode and modern Project Mode / class-based code.
related_updates: Recursive method/function calls remain fully supported and largely unchanged in current 4D versions, including in 4D's class-based (ORDA/Project Mode) methods
No newer 4D-specific construct has replaced recursion as a general control-flow technique
